config.effectiveWeightDecay: nginx also decays a failed peer's effective weight by weight/max_fails, so re-entry after fail_timeout ramps back in over a few requests
config.failureMetric: connection failures (rc!=0 / empty reply) instead of HTTP 5xx
config.loopbackRemovedBy: harness rm + systemctl reload nginx on both sides
config.probe: raw TLS 1.3 ClientHello with the configured SNI over the stream listener; ssl_preread selects the reality upstream
config.recoveryProbe: the recovery phase runs the whole window (120 probes every 0.5s); it does not stop at the first A
config.stableRecoveryRule: a side counts as recovered only when the trailing 20s of the complete window holds at least 3 A responses and the A chain reaching the newest one never gaps more than 10s (re-admission, not takeover: nginx ramps the peer's decayed effective weight back up)
config.upstreamCounters: per nginx worker; the upstream has no shared zone, so each worker removes the peer on its own

scenarioNote.perWorkerJitter: max_fails counters are per nginx worker (the upstream has no zone), so failure counts, removal instants and quiet stretches differ per worker. perWorkerJitter reports that spread; a single probe is one sample, not a global recovery time.
scenarioNote.recovery: first-A and stable-A are both recorded. The verdict uses stable-A; first-A is sampling bias when only some workers removed the peer.
